title: Kelly's blues and the Three Sixes
summary: Kelly was best on blues, including his own Three Sixes; Robinson played his last job with him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Did Chris know many different pieces or did he stick mostly to blues? People tell me he was very good on blues. Did he know a lot of other numbers too? Or what all did you play in the band?

How many numbers? Well he used to play different numbers but Chris had several blues there. He used to have blues there. He used to have blues there. I don't get how they go but he used to call it the three sixes.
Mm-hmm. Yeah. And that was the blues though. Yeah. One that he made up himself I guess.
He was good all right. He used to talk. It's been so long now I don't disremember because I had no... I used to know all them things but it doesn't flip me now. I've been putting him 30 years.
Well, that gives us a good idea of his style. That's better than most people. Most people just say, well, he used one of the flushers and they played blues and that's all they tell us.
Well, he used to play other pieces but his hobby was blues. He was the right time cornet player. That's all it did is story. To my judgment, he was good. I played the last job with him on earth.
